AKIEC.name: Actinic Keratosis / Bowen's Disease
clinical_features: Rough sandpaper or gritty palpable texture on skin surface
Persistent erythematous or yellowish-brown scaly macule or thin plaque
Typically located on chronic sun-exposed areas (head, face, scalp, forearms)
dermoscopic_features: Strawberry pattern: erythematous pseudo-network around hair follicles
Yellowish-white keratotic plugs filling follicle openings
Fine wavy rosettes under polarized light
Fine surface scale and crust
AKIEC.darker_skin_considerations: Erythema is often masked by melanin; lesions may present as mottled hyperpigmented macules or brownish-gray plaques with subtle scale. Pigmented Bowen's disease is more common and can simulate melanoma.
sources: Soyer HP et al., 'Dermoscopy of Actinic Keratosis and Bowen's Disease', JDDG 2015
Kittler H et al., 'Dermatoscopy: Pattern Analysis of Pigmented and Nonpigmented Lesions', 2nd Ed
Dadzie OE et al., 'Ethnic Dermatology: Principles and Practice', Ch. 14

BCC.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
clinical_features: Pearly translucent papule or nodule with rolled borders
Fine visible surface telangiectasia
Central ulceration, crusting, or non-healing bleeding sore
dermoscopic_features: Arborizing (tree-like) telangiectasias with distinct branching
Blue-gray ovoid nests and blue-gray globules
Spoke-wheel areas and leaf-like structures at periphery
Shiny white blotches and short crossing strands (crystalline structures)
Ulceration and small erosions
BCC.darker_skin_considerations: Over 50% of BCCs in Fitzpatrick IV-VI are pigmented (vs <10% in fair skin). They frequently present as brown-to-black nodules mimicking melanoma or seborrheic keratosis. Blue-gray nests, shiny white lines, and arborizing vessels remain key dermoscopic markers.
sources: Argenziano G et al., 'Dermoscopy of Basal Cell Carcinoma', Arch Dermatol 2002; 138(9):1157-1162
Bigby M et al., 'Pigmented basal cell carcinoma in dark-skinned individuals', JAAD 2004
Bolognia JL et al., 'Dermatology', 4th Ed, Ch. 108

BEN_OTH.name: Other Benign Lesions
clinical_features: Stable, non-progressive flesh-colored, yellowish, or brown papule or nodule
Smooth circumscribed margins with absence of spontaneous bleeding or rapid evolution
dermoscopic_features: Absence of melanoma-specific and malignant criteria
Homogeneous or structureless benign patterns
Regular linear or comma vessels without polymorphous atypia
BEN_OTH.darker_skin_considerations: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation or heavy melanin deposition can give benign papules (e.g. skin tags, cysts) a dark brown or black appearance, occasionally prompting unnecessary excision.
sources: Kittler H et al., 'Dermatoscopy', 2nd Ed
Bolognia JL et al., 'Dermatology', 4th Ed

BKL.name: Benign Keratosis (Seborrheic Keratosis / Solar Lentigo)
clinical_features: Well-demarcated 'stuck-on' waxy, verrucous, or velvety appearance
Uniform to variegated tan, brown, or black coloration
Dry, crumbly, or keratinaceous surface
dermoscopic_features: Milia-like cysts (small, round, bright white or yellowish spots)
Comedo-like openings / crypts (brown or black sharply circumscribed craters)
Gyri and sulci forming a brain-like (cerebriform) pattern
Hairpin vessels surrounded by a white halo
Fingerprint-like regular parallel delicate brown ridges
BKL.darker_skin_considerations: Frequently presents as Dermatosis Papulosa Nigra (DPN) on the face and neck of darker skin individuals as multiple small, smooth, hyperpigmented papules exhibiting cerebriform or comedo-like patterns.
sources: Braun RP et al., 'Dermoscopy of seborrheic keratosis', JAMA Dermatol 2002; 138(4):518-523
Babapour R et al., 'Dermatosis papulosa nigra: A review', JAAD 2017
Kittler H et al., 'Dermatoscopy', 2nd Ed

DF.name: Dermatofibroma
clinical_features: Firm, button-like dermal nodule commonly on lower extremities
Positive 'dimple sign' (central depression upon lateral pinch)
Hyperpigmented peripheral border with paler center
dermoscopic_features: Central white patch or scar-like structureless area
Delicate, uniform pigment network at the periphery
Occasional fine dotted or hairpin vessels in center
DF.darker_skin_considerations: In darker skin tones, the central area may exhibit marked post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation rather than classic white scar tissue; the peripheral network is frequently dense and dark brown.
sources: Zaballos P et al., 'Dermoscopic patterns of dermatofibroma: a study of 412 cases', Arch Dermatol 2008; 144(1):55-60
Bolognia JL et al., 'Dermatology', 4th Ed

INF.name: Inflammatory Condition (Eczema / Psoriasis / Lichen Planus)
clinical_features: Pruritic erythematous, violaceous, or hyperpigmented scaly macules/plaques
Ill-defined borders with excoriations (eczema) or sharply demarcated micaceous scale (psoriasis)
Polygonal flat-topped violaceous papules with Wickham striae (lichen planus)
dermoscopic_features: Uniformly distributed dotted vessels on a diffuse pink background (psoriasis)
Patchy dotted vessels with yellowish-orange serocrusts (eczema)
White crossing reticular lines (Wickham striae) with peripheral dotted/radial vessels (lichen planus)
Absence of pigment network or malignant tumor vessels
INF.darker_skin_considerations: Erythema rarely presents as bright red; it commonly appears as violaceous, gray, or dark brown hyperpigmented plaques. Post-inflammatory pigmentary alteration (hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation) is prominent and can obscure underlying vessel patterns.
sources: Errichetti E, Stinco G, 'Dermoscopy in General Dermatology: A Practical Overview', Dermatol Ther 2016; 6(4):471-507
Alexis AF et al., 'Dermatology for Skin of Color', 2nd Ed, McGraw-Hill

MAL_OTH.name: Other Malignant Lesions
clinical_features: Rapidly enlarging or indurated ulcerated nodule or plaque
Spontaneous bleeding, necrosis, or atypical infiltration
dermoscopic_features: Polymorphous and atypical vessels (corkscrew, looped, hairpin)
Shiny white lines and structureless areas
Irregular central necrosis or bleeding ulcerations
MAL_OTH.darker_skin_considerations: Atypical tumors (e.g. dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, atypical fibroxanthoma) can be misdiagnosed as benign keloids or cysts in darker skin due to firm subcutaneous feel and hyperpigmentation.
sources: Bolognia JL et al., 'Dermatology', 4th Ed
Lallas A et al., 'Dermoscopy of Rare Skin Tumours', Eur J Dermatol 2014

MEL.name: Melanoma
clinical_features: Asymmetry (shape and pigment distribution unequal across axes)
Border irregularity (scalloped, notched, or poorly defined edges)
Color variegation (multiple shades of brown, black, red, blue, or white)
Diameter frequently >6 mm, or rapid evolution in size, shape, or symptom
dermoscopic_features: Atypical pigment network with thick lines and irregular meshes
Irregularly distributed dots and globules of varying size
Blue-white veil (confluent blue-gray pigmentation with overlying ground-glass haze)
Atypical polymorphous vessels (corkscrew, dotted, serpentine)
Regression structures (peppering, white scar-like depigmentation)
Irregular peripheral streaks and pseudopods
MEL.darker_skin_considerations: Melanoma in darker skin individuals disproportionately occurs in acral sites (soles of feet, palms, nail beds - Acral Lentiginous Melanoma / ALM). Dermoscopy shows a characteristic parallel ridge pattern (pigment on ridges rather than furrows). Amelanotic variants can present as non-pigmented nodules mimicking pyogenic granuloma.
sources: Argenziano G et al., 'Seven-point checklist of dermoscopy: a new approach', Br J Dermatol 1998; 139:439-445
Bradford PT et al., 'Acral lentiginous melanoma: incidence and survival patterns in the United States', Arch Dermatol 2009; 145(4):427-434
Gloster HM, Neal K, 'Skin cancer in skin of color', JAAD 2006; 55(5):741-760

NV.name: Melanocytic Nevus (Common Mole)
clinical_features: Symmetric, uniformly pigmented tan, brown, or dark brown macule or papule
Smooth, round or oval, well-defined regular borders
Generally stable size under 6 mm without evolution
dermoscopic_features: Regular pigment network thinning out gradually at the periphery
Uniformly distributed dots and globules in center or concentric ring
Homogeneous brown or tan structureless background
Absence of atypical vessels, blue-white veil, or focal pseudopods
NV.darker_skin_considerations: In darker skin phototypes, normal nevi typically show denser and darker melanin pigmentation (dark brown to slate black) with intense contrast. Reticular and homogeneous dark patterns predominate and can be mistaken for dysplastic lesions if fair-skin baselines are applied.
sources: Kittler H et al., 'Dermatoscopy', 2nd Ed
Marghoob AA et al., 'Dermoscopic evaluation of nevi across diverse skin types', Semin Cutan Med Surg 2009

SCCKA.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Keratoacanthoma
clinical_features: Firm indurated hyperkeratotic nodule or plaque with central keratin crater
Rapid explosive growth over weeks (keratoacanthoma variant)
Frequent tenderness, scaling, and sun-exposed location
dermoscopic_features: Central amorphous keratin mass, crust, or ulceration
White circles surrounding hair follicle openings or dilated vessels
Hairpin and looped vessels surrounded by a distinctive white halo
Linear-irregular or serpentine atypical vessels
SCCKA.darker_skin_considerations: In patients with darker skin, SCC is the most common cutaneous malignancy and frequently arises in non-sun-exposed regions, chronic scars, burns (Marjolin ulcer), or chronic inflammatory ulcers. They are frequently pigmented and may mimic melanoma.
sources: Lallas A et al., 'Dermoscopy of Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Keratoacanthoma', Dermatol Pract Concept 2013; 3(2):61-68
Gloster HM, Neal K, 'Skin cancer in skin of color', JAAD 2006

VASC.name: Vascular Lesion (Hemangioma / Angioma / Pyogenic Granuloma)
clinical_features: Well-circumscribed bright red, violaceous, or blue-black papule or nodule
Blanches under diascopy (pressure) unless thrombosed
May bleed easily on minor friction
dermoscopic_features: Red, purple, or blue-black round/oval lacunae (vascular lagoons)
Pale whitish-pink fibrous septa separating lacunae
Reddish homogeneous structureless areas without pigment network
Absence of atypical branched vessels or melanin network
VASC.darker_skin_considerations: In darker skin tones, the lacunae frequently appear dark violaceous, dark blue, or deep black rather than bright ruby red; thrombosed hemangiomas and angiokeratomas can closely mimic nodular melanoma.
sources: Zaballos P et al., 'Dermoscopy of vascular lesions: a study of 422 cases', Arch Dermatol 2007; 143(3):329-335
Kittler H et al., 'Dermatoscopy', 2nd Ed
